To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rate of biotion uptake by HepG2 cells depends on biotin availability and that this is associated with changes in the amount of SMVT protein and its transcriptional activation.

Biotin availability is essential to maintain the expression of SMVT, the rate of biotropic transport in human liver cells, and the expression of biotin-dependent enzymes involved in biotic metabolism and biotic utilization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of SMVT gene transcription in human liver cells.
understanding the mechanisms involved in the regulation of SMVT expression and biotin uptake by human cells.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms involved in the regulation of the biotin utilization pathway in human cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SMVT is a key player in the regulation of biotinylation of carboxylases and the HCS-sCG-PKG pathway.
biotin availability controls SMVT gene transcription and the rate of [H]biotins transport in liver cells.
biotin availability regulates the expression of SMVT and its functional activity in human cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
biotin availability controls SMVT protein mass, mRNA expression levels, and the rate of uptake of this vitamin in human HepG2 liver cells through the activation of the HSC-sGC-PKG signaling pathway.
the biotin carrier SMVT is a target for biotin regulation in human cells and it may be a useful tool for the treatment of biotin deficiency.
SMVT is a biotin-responsive transporter that regulates the rate of biotic utilization in liver cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of biotic utilization in human cells is regulated by the availability of the vitamin.
biotin availability is a critical factor in the regulation of SMVT gene expression in HepG2 human liver cells.
biotin deficiency in humans may be associated with a reduction of the biotin uptake rate, which in turn may contribute to the impairment of the metabolic functions of the liver.
